## Purpose

`integration_adopt` records work that has *already* been delivered. Sometimes a
change reaches the default branch by a route the daemon did not drive — an
operator merged it by hand, a hotfix went straight in, work was rebased or
squashed by someone else. Those tasks are done, but the system has no delivery
journal entry for them, so they look undelivered forever and every later sweep
tries to carry them again.

Adoption closes that gap honestly. It proves the named ref really is at the SHA
the operator claims, checks each task's own source branch against that SHA, writes
one delivery journal row that says *an operator accepted this and it was not CI
attested*, and completes the tasks in child-before-parent order. It never replays
a repair, never re-pushes anything, and never pretends there was evidence there
was not. See [development integration](../../guides/development-integration.md).

## When a playbook uses it

It is an operator command. `_cmd_integration_adopt`
([`src/commands/integration_commands.py:1753`](../../../src/commands/integration_commands.py))
requires a LOCAL principal; the entry point is `aq integration adopt PROJECT_ID
--task … --head-sha … --reason …`
([`src/cli/integration.py:232`](../../../src/cli/integration.py)).

A playbook should not adopt on its own, because the interesting argument —
`accept_equivalent` — is a judgement about whether rewritten history still *is*
the task's work. When a task's branch is not an ancestor of the target SHA (a
squash, a rebase, a hand-applied patch), adoption refuses unless the operator
explicitly accepts equivalence. That acceptance is recorded per task in the
manifest as `operator_equivalent` rather than `ancestry`, so a later reader can
tell which tasks were proven and which were asserted.

## How it works internally

1. The contract is generated by the shared development registration
   ([`src/commands/contracts/integration.py:1946`](../../../src/commands/contracts/integration.py));
   `head_sha` must match a 40-character lowercase OID and `task_ids` must be
   non-empty at the model boundary
   ([`src/commands/contracts/integration.py:135`](../../../src/commands/contracts/integration.py)).
2. `_cmd_integration_adopt` (line 1753) requires a LOCAL principal and maps every
   service `ValueError`, `RuntimeError` or `KeyError` to `blocked`.
3. `DevelopmentIntegration.adopt`
   ([`src/integration/development.py:260`](../../../src/integration/development.py))
   requires a reason, a valid OID and at least one task, and the project must have
   a designated repository.
4. Under the repository exclusion lock it re-reads the remote: if `target_ref` is
   no longer at `head_sha`, adoption fails rather than recording a claim about a
   ref that has already moved.
5. For each task, in sorted order, it checks project and repository ownership,
   resolves the task's own branch on the remote, and asks whether that source is
   an ancestor of `head_sha`. Contained sources are recorded with
   `acceptance: ancestry`; sources that are not contained require
   `accept_equivalent` and are recorded as `operator_equivalent`.
6. Under `lock_hierarchy_project`, with the task rows locked `FOR UPDATE`, it
   refuses when any selected task still has a live session or an assigned agent
   (`DevelopmentBusy`), and when any child of a selected task is still open
   outside the selection.
7. It writes one `development_deliveries` row in state `adopted` carrying the
   manifest, the operator id, and evidence marked `operator_accepted` /
   `not_ci_attested`.
8. It orders the selection child-before-parent — failing on a cycle rather than
   guessing — and for each not-already-completed task writes a
   `task_completion_records` row (outcome `pass`, verification "Operator
   adoption; not CI attested", the adopted SHA as its commit) and applies the
   `COMPLETED` transition under an operator-adoption token. Blocked-flip,
   settled and ready notifications are flushed after the transaction.

## Side effects and persistence

One row in `development_deliveries`
([`src/database/tables.py:3839`](../../../src/database/tables.py)); one
`task_completion_records` row per task that was not already complete; and the
tasks themselves moved to `COMPLETED`, with their dependents unblocked by the
normal transition machinery.

No Git write happens at all. Adoption is a recording operation: the remote is
read to verify the claim and is never pushed to. Later sweeps then skip these
`(task_id, source_sha)` pairs, because a sweep treats `delivered` and `adopted`
journal rows identically when computing what is already done
([`src/integration/development.py:429`](../../../src/integration/development.py)).

## Failure modes and diagnostics

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `adopted` | The manifest was recorded and the tasks are complete. |
| `blocked` | The service refused; the message says why. |
| `unauthorized` | The caller is not a LOCAL operator. |

Messages worth recognising behind `blocked`:

- `target ref is no longer at the supplied SHA` — re-read the remote and retry
  with the current head.
- `<task>: source is not an ancestor; explicit equivalence acceptance required` —
  the branch was squashed or rebased; pass `accept_equivalent` if that is what
  happened.
- `task <id> does not belong to the repository project` — a task from another
  project or repository slipped into the selection.
- `selected tasks still have a worker assignment` — a worker still holds one of
  them; adoption will not close work out from under a live session.
- `required child <id> is still open` — a parent was selected while a child was
  not.
- `task hierarchy contains a cycle` — the selection's parent links are not a tree.

An invalid `head_sha` or an empty `task_ids` is rejected by the argument model
before the handler runs, and surfaces as `runtime_error`. Confirm adoption with
`aq integration status PROJECT_ID`, whose delivery receipts include the adopted
manifest.

## Example step

```markdown
2. Call `integration_adopt` with `project_id` `agent-queue`, `task_ids` bound to
   `hotfix.task_ids`, `target_ref` `refs/heads/main`, `head_sha` bound to
   `hotfix.head_sha`, and `reason` `operator merged the hotfix by hand`. An
   `adopted` outcome ends the rule; a `blocked`, `unauthorized`, `rejected` or
   `runtime_error` outcome fails it.
```
